subject: Private offer packaging and flexible commit options
messages:
From: Jeff Nolan <jeff.nolan@clearwave.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer packaging and flexible commit options

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile and the KV caching approach. We're evaluating a private offer for our platform (Clearwave) and have two logistics items where we need your help:

1) Packaging: We run both bursty evaluation workloads and steady-production inference. Our legal/procurement prefers a single SKU if possible but they also want consumption floors. Is there a recommended SKU that maps to reserved capacity + metered burst?

2) Channel margin: our reseller partner (CloudNorth) needs to know the gross margin band they should expect for this PO. They're pushing for a fixed 20% pass-through but we historically see a 12–18% range. Can you provide a channel margin schedule or sample waterfall we can include in the procurement packet?

If helpful I can share our expected 12-month consumption numbers (roughly 45M tokens/month baseline, 120M peaks). We'd like a draft private offer and an example amortization for partner margin.

Appreciate a short call next week if that's easier.

Best,
Jeff
Procurement Lead
Clearwave Systems
procure@clearwave.com

---
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jeff Nolan <jeff.nolan@clearwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer packaging and flexible commit options

Hi Jeff — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Ben (pricing/private offers) and Connor (deal ops) to build a short option set. Naomi and Soojin will chime on channel margin and marketplace pass-through mechanics.

High level: we can do a hybrid private offer that combines a reserved-capacity SKU (monthly commitment) with a metered burst SKU that bills at a slightly higher unit price. That lets you lock a baseline while keeping headroom for spikes. We'll attach a two-page draft and a channel-margin workbook for CloudNorth.

Action items for our side:
- Ben: produce 2 pricing scenarios (12-month commit with 10% off list; 24-month commit with tiered overage credits)
- Connor: confirm invoice pathing for reseller pass-through and tax treatment
- Naomi & Soojin: propose a channel margin schedule (gross and net waterfall) and note any marketplace listing caveats.

Jeff — can you send the 12-month consumption estimate and confirm whether CloudNorth will be the billed reseller or end-customer on the invoice? That determines how we model the margin waterfall.

I'll draft a short MA (mutual action) plan for the call.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer packaging and flexible commit options

Folks — attach is my initial thinking (I'll add to the shared workbook):

Scenario A (12-month):
- Baseline: reserve 30M tokens/month (node-hour equivalent) at $0.0008/token (10% off list)
- Overage: metered at $0.0012/token for consumption above baseline
- Early-adopter credit: 1% gross rebate if monthly spend > $60k for 3 consecutive months

Scenario B (24-month, deeper commit):
- Baseline: reserve 40M tokens/month at $0.00072/token (15% off list)
- Overage: $0.0010/token
- Commitment smoothing: allows reallocation every quarter within a 15% band

Channel margin guidance (quick):
- Gross pass-through target for CloudNorth: 12%–16% depending on commit depth
- If CloudNorth is reseller-of-record (they bill Clearwave): we recommend structuring a 14% fixed reseller fee plus a quarterly performance uplift (0–2%) tied to retention.
- If Clearwave bills and pays Redwood, CloudNorth can receive a referral/commission but margin to them will be lower (~8–10%).

I'll convert these into the channel_margin_summary.xlsx and outline the waterfall showing list -> net after reseller fee -> net after distribution taxes. Connor — any restrictions on invoice pathing?

Ben
Sr. Pricing Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: channel_margin_summary.xlsx (draft)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer packaging and flexible commit options

Quick ops note:
- We can support two invoice models: (1) Reseller-of-record (CloudNorth invoices Clearwave; Redwood invoices CloudNorth) or (2) Direct billing (Redwood invoices Clearwave, then Redwood pays CloudNorth commission).
- Tax handling: reseller-of-record is cleaner for VAT/OSS in EU; in the US the choice affects W9/1099 flows but both are supported.
- For the private offer (AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace) packaging: if you want a single-line item we typically create a composite SKU referencing reserved and burst units — the portal still treats them as two underlying SKUs but procurement sees a single line. That meets the "single SKU" ask without losing telemetry.

I'm happy to be on the call next Tue or Wed. Olga — propose Tue 10:00 PT?

Connor
Deal Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private offer packaging and flexible commit options

Jeff — thanks for the capacity estimate in your follow-up (you sent numbers to my calendar invite). Based on the team inputs above, attached is a short draft that contains:
- Two private-offer structures (Scenario A: 12-month hybrid commit; Scenario B: 24-month deeper commit) with unit economics
- A composite-SKU option that appears as one line on the marketplace/purchase order but maps to reserved + metered under the hood
- Channel margin waterfall (attached workbook) showing both reseller-of-record and direct-billing outcomes for CloudNorth

Highlights:
- If CloudNorth is reseller-of-record, a 14% reseller fee yields them ~12%–14% gross margin after distribution taxes (example in the workbook).
- For a single-line SKU we recommend the composite approach — it preserves telemetry and makes procurement reviews easier (we include the SKU mapping in the draft).
- Suggested next steps: 1) pick Scenario A or B, 2) legal to review attached private-offer draft, 3) finalize reseller billing model (reseller-of-record vs direct billing).

I've attached: Clearwave_PrivateOffer_Draft_v3.pdf and channel_margin_summary.xlsx (workbook has a tab with your 12-month consumption numbers prefilled).

If that looks good, let's take Tue 10:00 PT as the working session to finalize.

Best,
Olga
Director, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Clearwave_PrivateOffer_Draft_v3.pdf; channel_margin_summary.xlsx
